body:
`StirlingSeriesEM.lean`: Euler and Maclaurin on the unit interval for the logarithm. `tendsto_A` and `stirling_series`: the logarithm of the gamma function at a point with positive real part and imaginary part at least a half, minus Stirling's sum and half the logarithm of two pi, bounded by an explicit multiple of a power of the point's size, from the limit against the dependency's log-gamma sequence and Mathlib's Stirling. `StirlingSeriesBern.lean`: the Bernoulli functions bounded from their Fourier series. `StirlingSeriesPhase.lean` and `StirlingSeriesK5.lean`: the gamma phase from the series, and the sign of the completed zeta on the line through it. `StirlingSeriesPt49.lean` and `StirlingSeriesPt100.lean`: the signs at forty-nine and one hundred, certified this way, generated by `lean_stage3/checks/stirlingseries/gen_stirlingseries.py`.

**The cost.** The gamma side of a point costs `balls_new` 3 balls, against `balls_old_49` 515 at forty-nine and `balls_old_100` 2051 at one hundred on the old route, whose precision also had to grow with the height.

**Who wrote it.** One worker, `files` 10 files. The files were searched here for `sorry`, added axioms and `native_decide`, of which they have none, the package was rebuilt here, and each pin reads the standard axioms. Traps: TRAPS.md rows `trap_first` 141 to `trap_last` 145.

What remains. The horizon's slope term in Turing's lemma through the series, and the sign points up to the closing height.
